newsitem.title: FINLAND: RAISIO SEES 97 SALES AT FIM 5 BLN.
newsitem.headline: RAISIO SEES 97 SALES AT FIM 5 BLN.

text.p: Finnish foodstuffs, animal feed and chemicals group Raision Tehtaat Oy Ab said on Tuesday it expected its 1997 sales to reach five billion markka.

"Growing exports and new companies are expected to increase consolidated turnover considerably in the future, and the 1997 figure is expected to reach 5 billion markka," the company said in a statement with its final 1996 results.
Raisio's turnover in 1996 totalled 3.93 billion markka.
The company said with its preliminary results on February 13 the outlook for 1997 was clearly better than last year.

In Tuesday's statement, it said its strong financial position "continues to form a solid foundation for future operations, with growth prospects primarily in international business, through both exports and overseas manufacture.

"The margarine subdivision will be one of our key areas, with attention focusing particularly on maintaining and reinforcing the market position of Carlshamn Mejeri and on rapid improvements in the financial position of Raisio Polska Foods."
Carlshamn Mejeri is the Swedish margarine factory Raisio acquired last year as a launchpad for its Benecol cholesterol-reducing margarine in export markets.
It said on Tuesday its Polish margarine operation countered an otherwise favourable trend in the margarine subdivision.
Raisio said prospects for increasing exports by the foodstuffs division continued good.
"Business will increase in the chemicals division, in both Europe and America. Good prospects can be seen in the Far East, but more extensive operations there are unlikely before 1998," Raisio said.
"Market expectations for Benecol-related business continue to have an appreciable affect on the value of the entire Group," Raisio added.
